channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer 'not walking away' after local election mauling
item.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer accepted responsibility for Labour's poor Keir Starmer has said he takes "responsibility" for Labour's poor election performance, but also for putting matters right again. "I know I have my doubters and I know I need to prove them wrong, and I will," he said.

item.title: Ukraine reports Russian attacks and battlefield clashes despite ceasefire
item.description: Ukraine reported Russian attacks and battlefield clashes. Ukraine and ‌Russia agreed on May 8 to a ​ceasefire from May 9 to May 11 ⁠as part of a U. S.-led push for peace under President Donald Trump to end more than four years ‌of war since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.

item.title: Hantavirus, Covid, Norovirus, Legionnaires': Why Are Cruise Ships So Prone To Disease Outbreaks?
item.description: Cruise ships are designed environments where many people live, eat, Cruises are sold as floating holidays, but they are also useful for understanding public health. Cruise ships are carefully designed places where many people live, eat, relax and move through the same shared spaces for days at a time.

item.title: US and Mexico brace for heatwave as deadly floods hit South Africa
item.description: A heatwave is expected to intensify across the western United States and Mexico this Temperatures soar in California and Arizona, while deluge continues across Western and Northern CapeHeat is expected to intensify across western parts of the US and Mexico this week as a ridge of high pressure pushes temperatures well above the seasonal norm.

item.title: Pakistan PM announces to celebrate May 10 as ‘Marka-e-Haq Day’ every year
item.description: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced May 10 Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif claimed that Pakistani armed forces gave a "historic and befitting response" to the enemy, he said while addressing a ceremony on May 10, 2026, to mark the first anniversary of 'Marka-e-Haq'. Pakistan PM announces to celebrate May 10 as ‘Marka-e-Haq Day’ every year.

item.title: Film paints vision of a post-coup Brazil giving up rainforest
item.description: A fictional film depicts Brazil in 2025 following a successful rightwing coup. The plot shows the assassination of the president and the closure of congress. The new government then cedes control of the Amazon rainforest to the United States. The film highlights threats to Indigenous peoples.

item.description: Argentina is under scrutiny for hantavirus after authorities began tracing passengers from a Thirty years after first person-to-person transmission was documented in Patagonia, scientists say global heating could increase world’s exposureAn outbreak in rural communities 30 years ago in the Patagonia area of Argentina led scientists, for the first time, to document person-to-person transmission of hantavirus, which until then had been known only to spread through contact with rodents. item.title: Tehran, Taiwan, trade … what are the hazards facing Trump on Xi summit tightrope?
item.description: Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a summit with Chinese US leader enters talks with superpower rival from vulnerable position, but will be hoping for economic wins amid turbulent backdropIf all goes to plan over the next few days – and that is a big if – Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a highly anticipated summit with Xi Jinping, China’s leader. The trip will mark the first time a US president has visited China in nearly a decade.

item.title: Indonesian rescuers retrieve body from Mount Dukono as search continues
item.description: Indonesian rescuers recovered the body of a woman after a volcanic eruption on Mount Woman recovered after volcanic eruption on remote island, while operation to find two missing Singaporeans goes onRescuers have recovered the body of an Indonesian woman who was caught in a volcanic eruption on Mount Dukono on Indonesia’s remote island of Halmahera, officials have said. Search operations continued on Saturday for the bodies of two Singaporeans.

item.title: ‘Watching us is like watching a cousin’: the online creators reshaping Africa’s news ecosphere
item.description: Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa posted a TikTok video explaining a dispute between the South African and Rwandan presidents. She detailed the roles of various South African groups in a conflict. Jaxa's content focuses on current affairs for a South African audience. Africa is leading a change in news consumption habits – and transforming the lives of current affairs enthusiastsLast year Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa posted a TikTok video about South African peacekeepers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

item.title: Guardian reporter and colleagues detained and beaten by Somali police
item.description: Guardian reporter Mohamed Bulbul was detained and beaten by Somali police in Mogadishu. He was arrested with two colleagues, Abdihafid Nor Barre and Abdishakur Mohamed Moh. The arrests followed Bulbul's reporting for the Guardian on the alleged torture of a woman in prison.

item.title: Central African Republic: Funding cuts put humanitarian support at risk
item.description: Funding cuts threaten humanitarian operations in the Central African Republic. The Central African Republic (CAR) is making progress towards stability and security but major aid budget cuts threaten humanitarian operations there, a senior official with the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Friday in New York.

item.title: Wider hantavirus outbreak risk is ‘absolutely low’, insists UN health agency
item.description: The World Health Organization stated the risk of hantavirus spreading beyond the current cluster is very low. A flight attendant who had contact with an infected passenger tested negative for the disease. The passenger, from a cruise ship outbreak, later died.

item.title: Three hikers dead after Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcano erupts
item.description: Three hikers, two Singaporean and one Indonesian, died on Halmahera island after Mount Dukono erupted. They were in a restricted area when the volcano ejected an ash cloud approximately 10 kilometers high. No nearby villages were affected by the eruption.

item.title: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law on China spies in UK: ‘We’re not surprised’
item.description: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law stated he was unsurprised by reports of Chinese spies in the UK. The conviction of two men for spying, who had photographed Law, raises serious concerns about their access to sensitive information. Law lives with a bounty from Chinese authorities.
